The binary addition recurrence t(2n+j+b)=t(n+floor((j+b)/2)) XOR((j+b)mod2) gives residual transition (j,s)→(floor((j+b)/2),s XOR((j+b)mod2)), starting (c,0), output t(j) XOR s. Distinct j,s residuals are output-distinguishable because a period or anti-period for Thue–Morse would contradict alternating parity at numbers 2^h−p as h changes, including eventual periods. After e input bits u, reachable state is (floor((c+u)/2^e), t((c+u)mod2^e)); residue intervals yield v_e(c) and two exceptional coordinate-two corrections, while lower coordinates eventually contribute exactly four states. Disjoint upper-level first coordinates give the exact arbitrary-c sum; m≥2 sharp bounds follow from each v_e in [2,4] and explicit endpoint shifts. Independent BFS computed exact reachable pairs and matched the formula for every c=0..2047; finite checks support the symbolic all-c proof.
